Amid progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened. In line with the Fed’s average-inflation-targeting shift (Powell, Jackson Hole 2020) and rule-like guidance in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler, holding the funds rate at 0–0.25% with ongoing QE and forward guidance is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting principles (Svensson and Woodford) aimed at re-anchoring expectations at 2% while supporting the recovery (consistent with Romer and Romer’s evidence on the effects of monetary easing). Given pandemic-related supply shocks and the inflation-at-risk literature pointing to skewed upside risks during recoveries, the tone is mildly positive but cautious.
